newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares rise at noon on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares rise at noon on rebound.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices firmed at midday on Monday on a rebound following the extended falls of recent weeks due to Beijing's crackdown on excessive speculation, brokers said.
The A share index jumped 13.01 points or 3.02 percent to 444.10 on turnover of 4.4 billion yuan.
The B share index gained 2.96 points or 2.03 percent to 149.12 on turnover of HK$21.4 million.

"More investors now seem to be interpreting Beijing's recent clampdown as being aimed at fostering the long-term healthy development of the market rather than just bad news for equity investors," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.

China confirmed last Friday that it had replaced Zhou Daojiong, the chief of its top stock market watchdog China Securities Regulatory Commission, the latest of a string of harsh measures aimed at eliminating share trading irregularities.
Zhou Zhengqing, chairman of the Securities Commission under the State Council, or cabinet, had taken up an additional job as head of the market watchdog.
Beijing last week also announced tough penalities against several major financial institutions, including market heavyweight Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd, for speculative trading.
State banks, listed firms and state enterprises have been banned from engaging in speculative share trading.
"Investors have digested all the news and they think these policies will benefit the market over the long term," another analyst with a major Chinese securities firm said.

"The market seems to have bottomed out at current levels, although heavy selling pressure still looms in wake of the latest crackdown," the Guotai analyst said. "Turnover remained thin in the morning, indicating a cautious mood."
Brokers said they generally expected the A and B share markets to have more upside this week and expected B shares to continue to move closely in line with their A share counterparts.
"Investors think the worst of the news has now emerged and the time is ripe for a robust rebound," another analyst said.
On the B share market, toll road operator Guangdong Provincial Expressway was the best performer, surging HK$0.70 to its ten percent limit up of HK$7.68.
On the A share market, television tube maker SEG Zhongkang was the most actively traded share on volume of 30 million shares, adding 0.16 yuan to 15.25 yuan.
